## Your budget

You have 5 minutes and 40 tool calls for this task. A grep costs about 5
seconds, a test run can cost 30. Call get_status to see what remains.

Spend at most a third of your budget locating the code. Once you have a
plausible diagnosis, edit the source — a wrong patch scores the same as no
patch, so an unverified fix always beats an unfinished investigation. If
get_status shows half your time gone and you have not yet edited a source
file, stop investigating and make your best edit now.

## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Edit the source first. Only write a reproduction script once you have made
your edit and submitted it, and only if budget remains to run it.

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — everything left
in /workspace becomes your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py or
pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

The harness truncates what you receive: 5,000 characters from any command,
and 150 lines or 10,000 characters from read_file. A truncated result loses
information silently, so a broad read wastes a call AND leaves you guessing.

Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Then read_file with a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole
file and never cat one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "rich/cells.py", "content": "import re
from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Callable, List

from ._cell_widths import CELL_WIDTHS

# Regex to match sequence of the most common character ranges
_is_single_cell_widths = re.compile("^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$").match


@lru_cache(4096)
def cached_cell_len(text: str) -> int:
    """Get the number of cells required to display text.

    This method always caches, which may use up a lot of memory. It is recommended to use
    `cell_len` over this method.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to display.

    Returns:
        int: Get the number of cells required to display text.
    """
    _get_size = get_character_cell_size
    total_size = sum(_get_size(character) for character in text)
    return total_size


def cell_len(text: str, _cell_len: Callable[[str], int] = cached_cell_len) -> int:
    """Get the number of cells required to display text.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to display.

    Returns:
        int: Get the number of cells required to display text.
    """
    if len(text) < 512:
        return _cell_len(text)
    _get_size = get_character_cell_size
    total_size = sum(_get_size(character) for character in text)
    return total_size


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def get_character_cell_size(character: str) -> int:
    """Get the cell size of a character.

    Args:
        character (str): A single character.

    Returns:
        int: Number of cells (0, 1 or 2) occupied by that character.
    """
    return _get_codepoint_cell_size(ord(character))


@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def _get_codepoint_cell_size(codepoint: int) -> int:
    """Get the cell size of a character.

    Args:
        codepoint (int): Codepoint of a character.

    Returns:
        int: Number of cells (0, 1 or 2) occupied by that character.
    """

    _table = CELL_WIDTHS
    lower_bound = 0
    upper_bound = len(_table) - 1
    index = (lower_bound + upper_bound) // 2
    while True:
        start, end, width = _table[index]
        if codepoint < start:
            upper_bound = index - 1
        elif codepoint > end:
            lower_bound = index + 1
        else:
            return 0 if width == -1 else width
        if upper_bound < lower_bound:
            break
        index = (lower_bound + upper_bound) // 2
    return 1


def set_cell_size(text: str, total: int) -> str:
    """Set the length of a string to fit within given number of cells."""

    if _is_single_cell_widths(text):
        size = len(text)
        if size < total:
            return text + " " * (total - size)
        return text[:total]

    if total <= 0:
        return ""
    cell_size = cell_len(text)
    if cell_size == total:
        return text
    if cell_size < total:
        return text + " " * (total - cell_size)

    start = 0
    end = len(text)

    # Binary search until we find the right size
    while True:
        pos = (start + end) // 2
        before = text[: pos + 1]
        before_len = cell_len(before)
        if before_len == total + 1 and cell_len(before[-1]) == 2:
            return before[:-1] + " "
        if before_len == total:
            return before
        if before_len > total:
            end = pos
        else:
            start = pos


# TODO: This is inefficient
# TODO: This might not work with CWJ type characters
def chop_cells(text: str, max_size: int, position: int = 0) -> List[str]:
    """Break text in to equal (cell) length strings, returning the characters in reverse
    order"""
    _get_character_cell_size = get_character_cell_size
    characters = [
        (character, _get_character_cell_size(character)) for character in text
    ]
    total_size = position
    lines: List[List[str]] = [[]]
    append = lines[-1].append

    for character, size in reversed(characters):
        if total_size + size > max_size:
            lines.append([character])
            append = lines[-1].append
            total_size = size
        else:
            total_size += size
            append(character)

    return ["".join(line) for line in lines]


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover

    print(get_character_cell_size("😽"))
    for line in chop_cells("""这是对亚洲语言支持的测试。面对模棱两可的想法，拒绝猜测的诱惑。""", 8):", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 150, "total_lines": 154, "is_truncated": true}
